elements.element: Renewal occurs only by mutual written agreement (preferred branch 1)
elements.evidence: "may be renewed for additional periods of twelve (12) months each only by mutual written agreement of the parties"
No automatic renewal language; renewal requires affirmative mutual written agreement — permitted alternative not selected, so not required

elements.element: Alternative branch: Customer opt-out on 30 days' notice
elements.evidence: No opt-out mechanic; condition absent because renewal is not automatic

elements.element: Alternative branch: Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal
elements.evidence: No reminder obligation; not required under the mutual-agreement branch

elements.element: Renewal price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%
elements.evidence: "any increase in fees for a renewal period shall not exceed the lesser of the increase in CPI over the prior period and three percent (3%)"
Clause makes renewal contingent on "mutual written agreement of the parties"; no auto-renewal

elements.element: Non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days (fallback)
elements.evidence: No non-renewal notice window stated anywhere in the edited clause
"shall not exceed the lesser of the increase in CPI over the prior period and three percent (3%)"

offending_extra_words: for additional periods of twelve (12) months each
reasons: The preferred level is satisfied via its first permitted alternative: renewal only by mutual written agreement, plus the lesser-of-CPI-and-3% cap on renewal fee increases. The unilateral seven-year Licensor option is removed, which is the core customer protection.

Fallback is not satisfied and need not be: there is no automatic renewal and no non-renewal notice window, so the 60-day window element fails. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains and the preferred bargain is complete.

Minimality fails: the fixed "additional periods of twelve (12) months each" is imported from the automatic-renewal alternative and is unnecessary where renewal requires mutual written agreement each time; a tighter replacement (mutual written agreement + fee cap) would suffice. The official minimality gate also flags the 19→48 word expansion and 0.70 changed-character ratio.

Intent is preserved: the breach-termination sentence, Licensor's retained payment rights, and Article IV.II/III mutual-extension mechanics remain effective, and no undefined term or contradiction is introduced (the 12-month renewal periods sit consistently alongside IV.II/III).
